title: On Improving the Cohesiveness of Graphs by Merging Nodes: Formulation, Analysis, and Algorithms

problem.claim: The work studies improving graph cohesiveness by merging nodes, using the size of the k-truss for a given k as the objective.

gap.claim: Node merging has been overlooked as an operation for enhancing graph connectivity and robustness.

contributions.claim: The problem is mathematically formulated with the size of the k-truss as the objective.
The work establishes NP-hardness and non-modularity of the problem.
BATMAN is developed to select sets of nodes for merging, based on theoretical findings and empirical observations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that BATMAN is superior to several baselines in speed and effectiveness.
The reported comparison uses extensive experiments on fourteen real-world graphs.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graphs model real-world structures, and highly connected and robust structures are desirable in many applications.
Edge addition and node anchoring have been studied for improving connectivity and robustness, while node merging has been overlooked.
The work formulates graph cohesiveness improvement through node merging using k-truss size as the objective.
The problem's NP-hardness and non-modularity are established, followed by development of the BATMAN node-merging algorithm.
BATMAN is compared with several baselines on fourteen real-world graphs for speed and effectiveness.

unknowns: The abstract does not describe the BATMAN algorithm's specific operations or guarantees.
The abstract does not provide quantitative experimental results or details about the baselines.
